source_provenance.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production enemy sprite motion atlas, transparent PNG, exactly sixteen full-body animation frames.
Input image 1 is a STYLE AND IDENTITY REFERENCE. Use ONLY the TOP-LEFT creature in this reference sheet. Ignore and never borrow anatomy, colors, wings, tails or weapons from the other nine creatures. The top-left creature is the canonical M01 辉砂虫族: a dangerous nonhuman hulking amber/coral beetle-mantis insect with a low rounded segmented golden amber abdomen, orange-coral armored shell plates edged in pale ivory and old brass, glistening amber shell nodules, a small forward insect head with large jade/teal compound eyes, two delicate backward-curled brass antennae, SIX jointed insect walking legs ending in six pointed feet, and a separate pair of huge curved ivory-gold scythe forelimbs. No humanoid anatomy, no clothing, no fists, no human legs. Preserve this exact character in every frame, not sixteen different insects. A dangerous predatory insect, not a cute pet.
LOCKED STANDARD: bright hand-painted cartoon fantasy, classical ruins combined with magical steam machinery, high camera three-quarter oblique overhead view, nearly isometric composition, 2.5D solid volume, warm sunshine inside the character surfaces and fresh vivid colors. Maintain crisp deep-plum contour edges, tactile painted facets, amber/coral/pale ivory/gold shell, jade compound eyes. Dark creases between hard shell plates, soft warm top-left highlights. Rich physical volume and thickness rather than flat icon shapes or photorealism.
ATLAS LAYOUT: square target 2048 x 2048 canvas, invisible precise 4 columns x 4 rows of equal 512 x 512 cells. Strict row-major index0–15 left-to-right then top-to-bottom. EXACTLY sixteen separate complete sprites. Every frame faces SCREEN RIGHT: the jade-eyed head is on the right and abdomen on the left, seen from consistent high three-quarter camera. Same anatomical body size and proportions in all frames. Walks IN PLACE. All six walking feet and both full curved scythes, antenna tips and full abdomen fit within their own cell. Sprite footprint including all appendages at most 60 percent of cell width and height. Leave at least 20 percent empty TRANSPARENT gutter on all four sides. Do not crop, overlap neighbors, or touch any cell edge. Normal body crown-to-ground height about 38 percent of cell height, excluding raised scythes and antennae. Ground/foot anchor near local x=256,y=370 for every cell; same global body scale. Deep anticipation and recoil can bend the body, but never resize it. Invisible grid, no labels or frame numbers.
The SIX distinct walking feet must remain complete and separate in every pose: three near-side feet and three far-side feet, visibly staggered so they can be counted. Keep pair of large scythe forelimbs in front, visually distinguishable from the six walking feet. Vary actual joint bends and planted versus lifted feet across the walk cycle. The stable armored abdomen is never recolored or changed.
ROW1 frame0–3: first half of an eight-phase alternating-tripod insect walking cycle, six legs moving anatomically in place.
0 neutral contact/idle-compatible stance: near front foot forward and near rear foot back, middle near foot braced; complementary far leg tripod supports the abdomen, paired scythes held in threatening low forward guard.
1 first tripod compresses: planted joints bend down under weight, complementary three feet begin lift, shell lowers very slightly.
2 passing: lifted near front/far middle/near rear legs tuck and pass under body, other three feet fully planted, scythes counterbalance subtly.
3 first tripod reaches forward: those three swing feet extend forward with toes lifted, other tripod holds body, shell lifts slightly.
ROW2 frame4–7: second half of the same continuous eight-phase cycle, visibly opposite leg sequence.
4 opposite tripod contact: far front foot now forward, near middle and far rear support; other leg positions reverse frame0.
5 opposite tripod compresses: opposite three planted joints flex, previous support feet lift, tiny downward shell motion.
6 opposite passing: far front/near middle/far rear swing beneath shell while the other tripod anchors, scythes subtly counter-swing.
7 opposite reach: opposite three swing feet extend in preparation for contact, abdomen rises slightly and returns smoothly to frame0.
Do not make eight copies of the same stance. Each walk pose must have distinct foot placements, knee bends and tripod phase while shell dimensions remain constant.
ROW3 frame8–11: paired scythe attack, each silhouette decisively different.
8 windup start: wide six-foot brace, torso tilts backward, BOTH scythe forelimbs lift upward diagonally, elbows curl in preparation.
9 full windup/locked attack anticipation: both huge scythes raised high and back above head, sharp tips wholly inside cell, head pulled back, six feet fully braced. Clear overhead threatening silhouette.
10 release: forceful DOWNWARD-FORWARD DOUBLE SCYTHE SLASH, both large blades sweep down ahead to the right near ground height, insect body pitches forward, six legs brace. Do not add action trails or effects. Blades visibly low, not raised.
11 recovery: blades rise partly from the downslash into forward guard, shell halfway straightens, six feet settle centered.
ROW4 frame12–15: a four-frame hurt recoil and settle sequence.
12 initial hit recoil: head and shell snap backward to the left, scythes recoil inward, six legs splay to catch balance, no added damage effect.
13 deepest recoil: shell leans back and compresses, head pulls back markedly, hind feet plant harder and front feet recoil, lowered scythes protect body. Same character size.
14 regain balance: abdomen and head return halfway forward, middle legs recover, scythes move back toward guard.
15 hurt settle: stable threatening right-facing low guard, six feet regain ordinary tripod-ready stance and armor/head return toward walk0.
TRANSPARENCY: real alpha-zero transparent background outside exact insect silhouettes, no opaque square, no floor, no ground planes, no cast shadows, no contact shadows, no drop shadows, no halo, no glow outside the insect, no scene or ruins painted in the atlas. Warm illumination is painted INSIDE the sprites only. No particles, slash streaks, impact flashes, blood, UI, labels, text, frame numbers, borders, grid, watermark or extra objects. Six feet and paired scythes wholly visible, no missing limbs, no extra walking legs, no flying insect, no cropped anatomy. All sixteen are the SAME canonical top-left amber/coral jade-eyed insect in distinct poses, right-facing high three-quarter view.
